*** SPRINT 73 / V0.29.28 -- 2 of 4 DONE (US-549 I-043, US-550 I-044). REMAINING: US-543 (A-4 Pi<->server parity guard, 6 assertions, M) and US-545 (A-18 BT bond self-heal, M). Both are M and neither is a documented blocker -- pick US-543 next by priority order. ***

*** READ THIS FIRST -- IT WILL COST YOU A STORY IF YOU DON'T: THE GREP TOOL CANNOT SEE specs/UI/dist/. *** That directory is gitignored-but-TRACKED, and the Grep tool is ripgrep-backed, so it honours .gitignore and skips the entire shipped UI kit. Sweeping for `%U` across the repo with Grep returned ZERO hits while all five defect sites were sitting right there. An empty result read like 'already fixed'. `git grep -n <pattern>` searches tracked files and found all five instantly. GENERALISE IT: an empty search result is evidence only if you have established the tool can see the files. US-543 is a repo-wide contract audit -- use git grep for it, not Grep.

US-550 AS BUILT: `%U` -> `__PI_UID__` on the 5 kiosk units that declare XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, resolved at install time by a new V-4 probe (`id -u $PI_USER`) in both kit installers, next to the existing __PI_USER__ (V-1) / __CHROMIUM_BIN__ (V-3) seams. Dry-run now renders the resolved dir (`/run/user/1000`), which is the only off-Pi evidence the substitution actually reaches the template. V-4 runs LAST of the four probes on purpose so V-1/V-2/V-3 keep their abort precedence. An unresolvable uid ABORTS -- never falls back to 0, which would reinstate I-044 silently (unit installs, chromium starts, only the journal knows).

THE SET WAS 5, NOT THE 6 THE ISSUE LISTED -- dashboard.service.x11 never declared XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. So the guard DISCOVERS units by globbing both kit dirs and pins the count, rather than trusting a list. Do the same in US-543: name the table set by construction (sync_log.PK_COLUMN, as its DoD already says) so a future synced table is covered the day it lands.

*** THE LESSON I MOST WANT YOU TO HAVE: A FORCED-OVERRIDE TEST PROVES THE OVERRIDE WORKS AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE REAL PATH. *** Mutation C (`id -u ... || echo 0` -- the exact silent fallback the story forbids) stayed GREEN. My fail-loud test set FORCE_UID empty, which short-circuits at the override branch and never runs `id -u` at all: I had tested the mock, not the mechanism. Fixed by adding a test that UNSETS the override and names a user that cannot exist, so the genuine probe runs and genuinely fails; under mutation C it goes red printing `/run/user/0`, i.e. it reproduces the original defect. Every FORCE_*/mock-driven suite in this repo is worth re-reading with that question: does anything exercise the path that runs on the Pi? US-545's BT work is ALL mock-driven -- this trap is waiting there.

SECOND LESSON, five sprints running: DECLARATION != MECHANISM. Mutation B (drop the __PI_UID__ sed) left the installer PRINTING 'Resolved user UID: 4242' while shipping a literal `/run/user/__PI_UID__`, and my static test (placeholder + `id -u` + FORCE_UID all appear in the file) stayed green -- those strings survive in comments. Only the end-to-end dry-run render caught it.

TOKENIZE, and note the US-522 substring lesson INVERTS here: the fixed units now explain %U in their own headers on purpose, so `'%U' not in text` would fail on a CORRECT file (false positive, not false negative). The guard parses Environment= assignments (comments stripped FIRST, continuations joined) and asserts on the value. Absence assertion => the parser carries a positive control (must still FIND a planted /run/user/%U) and a negative one (a commented-out directive must NOT parse as live); mutation D (parser returns {}) took 3 red headed by that control.

4 MUTATIONS, reverted BY HAND (git checkout is outside the allow-list), byte-exact per `git diff --numstat` -- every unit file reads +N/-1, i.e. the one Environment line plus header, no residue.

COLLATERAL, FLAGGED NOT HIDDEN: 3 existing test files needed the one-line treatment V-3 got when IT landed (`env.setdefault(*_FORCE_UID, '1000')` beside the existing FORCE_CHROMIUM setdefault). A new mandatory install-time probe breaks every off-Pi harness whose forced user ('pi', 'tunerbox') does not exist on a dev box. No assertion was weakened. Also folded the substitution set into one `render_unit()` per installer -- it was about to become a third copy of the same sed, which is how a placeholder lands on the install path but not the dry-run path.

GATE: targeted = tests/deploy/test_kiosk_runtime_dir.py (16) + the 4 suites sharing these artifacts (test_kiosk_install, test_splash_kit, test_dashboard_kit, test_deploy_pi) = 140 passed, EXIT 0, green again after every revert. ruff clean on all 4 touched .py files.

ENVIRONMENT (all still true): `make` is NOT on PATH -- exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`. pytest config SUPPRESSES the `N passed` line, so grepping for 'passed' returns NOTHING on a clean run -- trust the exit code. Glob over the repo root TIMES OUT (SMB share); `git ls-files | grep` is instant. Bash rejects multi-operation `&&` chains and `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`; a bare `VAR=x cmd ...` invocation needed `bash -c '...'` to get approved.

STILL OWED, Pi-side (both splash stories now carry one; batch them on the next deploy+boot): US-550 -- `systemctl show splash-boot.service -p Environment -p User` must read /run/user/1000, NOT /run/user/0, and `journalctl -u splash-boot.service` must be clean of dconf/'Could not parse server address'. ASSERT AGAINST `systemctl show`, NOT THE UNIT TEXT -- trusting the unit text is precisely why I-044 existed. US-549 -- `journalctl -u splash-grace.service | grep '[shutdown-splash] terminal'` on the next clean shutdown, BEFORE spending a real AC-loss event on the reverse-splash drill. Prior sprint's F-126 debts + the I-us536 autoRotateS:0 resolver defect are unchanged and still open (offices/ralph/archive/ + the PM issues folder).
